corrected_draft.description_medium: An Associated Press report published April 18, 2017, said Ivanka Trump’s company received provisional approval from China on April 6 for three trademarks covering jewelry, bags and spa services. corrected_draft.description_long: An Associated Press report published April 18, 2017, said Ivanka Trump’s company received provisional approval from China on April 6 for three trademarks covering jewelry, bags and spa services. That evening, Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner attended a Mar-a-Lago dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife. The report distinguished the three approvals announced for that date from the wider trademark portfolio: it said the company then had 16 registered trademarks in China and 32 pending applications, and that four marks had received preliminary approval since the inauguration. Thus, “16” described registered marks overall, not the number newly approved on April 6. The article also discussed the family’s stated ethics safeguards and concerns raised by former government ethics officials about business and policy overlap. This draft reports the discrete trademark approval and dinner chronology, without treating the timing as proof of improper influence or asserting that all 16 marks were granted that day.

corrected_draft.title: OPM proposes Schedule Policy/Career rule covering an estimated 50,000 roles
corrected_draft.description_short: OPM proposed Schedule Policy/Career; White House estimated 50,000 roles could eventually qualify.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On April 18, 2025, the White House said OPM had proposed a Schedule Policy/Career rule for policy-influencing career roles. The administration estimated that 50,000 positions might eventually qualify. The proposal did not itself transfer any employee into the category; future movement depended on a final rule and later executive action.
corrected_draft.description_long: The White House fact sheet said OPM estimated that 50,000 positions, about 2 percent of the federal workforce, could ultimately be moved into Schedule Policy/Career. It also stated that the proposed rule did not itself move any positions; transfers would occur only through a later executive order after a final rule. The category was described as career positions filled through existing merit-based hiring, with employees expected to implement the law and administration policies. The fact sheet said covered roles could lose access to some adverse-action procedures and appeals, while line employees such as Border Patrol agents and wage-and-hour inspectors would generally be excluded. This was an OPM proposal and estimate, not evidence that 50,000 employees had already been reclassified or that an actual list of “disloyal” workers had been created. The narrow event is the administration’s April 18 announcement of the proposed rule.

remaining_gap: The White House fact sheet describes a proposed OPM rule and an estimate, not an immediate Jan. 20 removal or completed reclassification. Limit to the April 18 proposal.
